- [FACT] NCAT is the NSW Civil and Administrative Tribunal that decides a range of civil and administrative cases in New South Wales.
- [FACT] NCAT commenced operation on 1 January 2014, consolidating the work of 22 former tribunals into a single point of access for specialist tribunal services in NSW.
- [FACT] The law that establishes NCAT and governs its operations is the Civil and Administrative Tribunal Act 2013.
- [FACT] NCAT provides a simple, quick, and effective process for resolving disputes and reviewing administrative action.
- [FACT] NCAT offers services and processes to support self-representation by parties in most matters, plain language forms and documents, simplified processes, and a range of alternative dispute resolution methods.
- [FACT] The types of cases dealt with by NCAT include tenancy issues, building works, decisions on guardianship, and administrative review of government decisions.
- [FACT] NCAT's jurisdiction and case types are managed through its Divisions.
- [FACT] NCAT's Appeal Panel provides a mechanism for prompt reviews of most Tribunal decisions.
- [FACT] NCAT's jurisdiction and diverse case types are managed through its four Divisions and the Appeal Panel.
- [FACT] To apply to NCAT, one must identify the case type and complete an application form.
- [FACT] Parties should start preparing for their hearing upon receiving a notice of hearing from NCAT.
- [FACT] NCAT uses alternative resolution processes to help parties resolve disputes before the hearing.
- [FACT] After the hearing, NCAT will make a decision and orders.
- [FACT] Certain Tribunal decisions can be internally appealed to the NCAT Appeal Panel.
- [FACT] The Consumer and Commercial Division of NCAT resolves disputes such as tenancy and other residential disputes, and consumer claims.
- [FACT] The Consumer and Commercial Division deals with various case types, including housing and property, tenancy, social housing, boarding houses, residential communities, holiday parks, agricultural tenancy, strata schemes, community schemes, home building, retirement villages, dividing fences, consumer claims, motor vehicles, retail leases, agent commissions and fees, conveyancing costs, and pawnbrokers and second-hand dealers.
- [FACT] The Appeal Panel determines internal appeals from decisions made by NCAT's Divisions.
- [FACT] The Appeal Panel
